newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-SFE wheat edges higher, seen firming.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-SFE wheat edges higher, seen firming.

text.p: Wheat futures edged up on the Sydney Futures Exchange (SFE) on Wednesday as the market began to look like turning up, brokers said.
The most frequently-traded January contract rose by A$1.50 to A$181.50 on seven trades while the March contract fell by 50 cents to A$181.00 on five trades.
"Technically speaking, the market is telling me that it wants to go up," said Colin Lethbridge of ANZ McCaughan Futures.
The market had reached a very interesting stage in the last couple of days, he said.
"Outside range" trading in the U.S. on Monday was a strong indicator of a change of direction, he said.
The overnight rally taking December wheat to US$4.52/bushel broke the downtrend, he said.
USDA figures due out later on Wednesday for supply/demand provided good reason to be nervous, Lethbridg said. "However, the technicals are telling that the seasonal low is in place."
The SFE had corresponded to U.S. market moves by lifting January wheat in recent days, he said.
A gain to A$187 or A$188 for January wheat would confirm the breaking of the downtrend in Australia, he said.
